skill.name: subagent-driven-development
skill.description: Coordinates implementation plan execution by using fresh subagents for each task, then requiring spec compliance and code quality reviews before moving on.
skill.summary: Runs each implementation task through an implementer, a spec reviewer, and a code quality reviewer.

content.value_statement: Complex implementation plans lose quality when one context handles every task. This skill coordinates fresh subagents for implementation, spec checks, and code quality reviews.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use same-session subagent execution for independent plan tasks.
Provides implementer, spec reviewer, and code quality reviewer prompt templates.
Defines review loops for missed requirements, extra work, and quality issues.
Shows a task-by-task workflow with testing, commits, and re-review steps.
Lists red flags that prevent skipping reviews or moving ahead with open issues.
limitations: Requires a written implementation plan before the workflow starts.
Works best when tasks are mostly independent and can be reviewed separately.
Does not run agents automatically; the user must dispatch them.
Adds extra review steps, which can increase token use and elapsed time.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Feature Plan
use_cases.description: Break a planned feature into reviewed implementation tasks inside one AI session.

use_cases.title: Control AI Coding Work
use_cases.description: Use fresh subagents to reduce context drift while preserving review checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Verify Contract Compliance
use_cases.description: Compare each delivered task against its requirements before quality review begins.

prompt_templates.title: Run One Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use subagent-driven development for the next task in my plan. Dispatch an implementer, then run spec and quality reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Execute a Small Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute this three-task plan with fresh subagents. Give each subagent full task text, required context, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Review Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: When a reviewer finds issues, return to the same implementer for fixes. Re-review until both reviewers approve.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Release Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute all independent tasks in this branch plan. Track status, collect commit SHAs, and finish with a final code review.

output_examples.input: A user asks to execute task one from a prepared implementation plan.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a task handoff, requests implementation, runs spec review, runs quality review, and marks the task complete.

output_examples.input: A reviewer finds an extra feature that was not requested.
output: The implementer removes the extra work.
The spec reviewer checks the corrected task again.
The workflow continues only after approval.

output_examples.output: The workflow sends the whole branch for final review and then moves to the finishing branch process.

best_practices: Paste full task text into each subagent prompt instead of making the subagent read the plan.
Resolve spec compliance issues before starting code quality review.
Keep one implementer responsible for fixing issues found in its task.
anti_patterns: Starting several implementation subagents for overlapping tasks in parallel.
Accepting an implementer report without reading the actual changed code.
Moving to the next task while review issues remain open.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides a same-session workflow for implementing planned tasks with fresh subagents and two review stages.

faq.question: Does it write code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and prompt templates; your AI tool performs the actual work.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it when the work is exploratory, tightly coupled, or lacks a written implementation plan.

faq.question: Why use fresh subagents?
faq.answer: Fresh subagents reduce context carryover and keep each task focused on its own requirements.

faq.question: What reviews are required?
faq.answer: Each task gets spec compliance review first, then code quality review after spec approval.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
